route_base_note: Current Office uses hash routes. The design-foundation slice moves to a stable /office browser base while preserving these logical routes.

CAP-011.name: Factory Office
CAP-011.job: Register Projects, create and inspect Actions, follow Lead/Campaign work, inspect candidates and quality evidence, configure providers and runtime policy, and manage secure browser/device access.
user_actions: register a Project
configure Project paths, capabilities, quality profile and active state
create a frozen Action with typed checks
create and revoke a scoped delegation
submit, assess, freeze and explicitly start a Lead request
create, authorize, queue and cancel a Campaign
queue a Run Attempt
inspect candidates, receipts, gate, sessions, cleanup and usage
configure, test and revoke provider credentials
enable or disable the semantic-review policy
inspect an Action specification, checks and related Core work
inspect recorded participants in a visual floor, table and timeline with a shared inspector
follow a participant to its Campaign, WorkUnit, Run, Attempt, candidate and Gate evidence
inspect bounded, redacted provider tool events for an exact session generation
enroll and revoke browser sessions, create a device pairing challenge, and approve or reject a pending phone
connect a GitHub credential, inspect its verified login/scopes and revoke it
bind one owner/repository and default branch per Project
run a bounded GitHub issue sync and inspect truthful sync, stale and rate-limit state
search, filter and page synchronized issues and read an issue body as untrusted plain text
CAP-011.notes: The current UI polls Core; no SSE/live-stream claim. Browser authorization uses HttpOnly device-session cookies and a readable CSRF cookie, never browser storage bearer tokens. QR pairing includes only a non-authorizing challenge identifier; phone sessions remain pending until owner approval and verification-code confirmation. The service worker is network-only and does not cache Core API responses or authorize offline work. Core reports CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, UNKNOWN or DISABLED from its private Office health projection; this does not prove mobile-network reachability. Overview, Decision Inbox, Action detail, the tabbed Campaign workspace, Runtime, Settings, Access & Devices, Agent Office and the read-only Issues snapshot foundation are implemented. Agent Office projects recorded participants only. Issues has an encrypted GitHub connection, one repository binding per Project, per-page ETag sync with credential-generation fencing and credential-wide backoff, stable issue identity and safe plain-text detail; governed intake, board ordering, Action/Campaign relationships, issue writing and a real authorized GitHub call remain later work. The Issues view is wired at /issues and component-tested; real browser acceptance remains pending. Docs remain a later slice.

CAP-049.name: Operational Overview and Decision Inbox
CAP-049.job: See authoritative Core state, inspect blocked work and unresolved usage, and act only through explicit Core operations.
user_actions: inspect authorized campaigns, blocked work, decisions, measured spend, recent accepted candidates and recent events
open the Decision Inbox and follow each item to its authoritative module
resolve an AMBIGUOUS or UNKNOWN Core model call with an explicit operator reason
inspect an Action frozen specification, checks and related Campaigns, Lead requests and delegations
CAP-049.notes: Overview and decisions are operator-authenticated Core projections; the client does not synthesize decisions. The Inbox exposes model-call resolution and navigation only. Campaign authorization and Gate repair remain on their existing module pages. No SSE or live-stream claim.

CAP-050.name: Campaign operational workspace
CAP-050.job: Understand and inspect a Campaign end to end from authorization through WorkGraph, execution, candidates, evidence, Gate, budget and recovery.
user_actions: inspect the Campaign objective lifecycle WorkGraph Runs Attempts sessions candidates evidence Gate budget and recovery
deep-link directly to the WorkGraph Execution Candidates Evidence Gate Budget or Events tab
load the bounded candidate Git diff summary for the recorded revision
cancel a Campaign after an explicit consequence confirmation
inspect the interactive WorkGraph dependency layout and select a WorkUnit
follow a selected WorkUnit to its exact Run, Attempt, participant session, candidate, receipts and Gate
CAP-050.notes: Campaign authorization, Run state, Attempt state and Gate outcome are displayed separately. The WorkGraph now includes a deterministic dependency layout, keyboard selection and a WorkUnit inspector while preserving the authoritative table. Graph presentation states are explicitly derived from recorded task status and dependencies; malformed data is surfaced, not repaired. Candidate diff metadata is bounded to changed paths and diff stat; source bodies are not rendered. Participant, tool-event and visual Office projections are provided by Agent Office.

CAP-051.name: Runtime operational console
CAP-051.job: Inspect Core health, registered Workers, provider sessions, model-call usage, reserved ceilings, cleanup, telemetry and runtime policy without terminal inspection.
user_actions: inspect Core health and registered Worker records
filter provider sessions by state usage cleanup worker or route
inspect recent and unresolved model-call reservations with measured usage and reservation ceiling
release an AMBIGUOUS or UNKNOWN reservation with an explicit audited reason
inspect telemetry export and semantic-review policy
CAP-051.notes: Sampled measured spend covers usage-known sessions and the latest 200 model calls. Reserved ceiling uses unresolved model-call max cost plus open provider-turn max cost. Unmeasured session count is shown separately; session cost is not claimed as a held ceiling. Supervisor, nested Podman and broker state are not exposed by the current Core API and are shown as unavailable, never inferred. Reservation release is explicit; no automatic release exists.

CAP-052.name: Provider and runtime Settings workspace
CAP-052.job: Configure Core-owned provider routes, credentials, models, limits and review policy while distinguishing configuration, connection testing and proven coding inference.
user_actions: inspect provider authentication status model endpoint auth modes and ChatGPT OAuth state
save or replace a provider credential without reading it back
revoke a credential after explicit consequence confirmation
set the default route and advanced token cost and rate limits
test provider model discovery without claiming coding inference
enable or disable semantic review policy and inspect configuration audit history
CAP-052.notes: Credentials are encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser. A saved route is not proof of access. A connection test reads the provider model list only and is not coding inference. ChatGPT OAuth remains visibly blocked or not applicable. Provider revisions do not rewrite frozen Campaign bindings.

CAP-045.name: Container-native Compose installation
CAP-045.job: Install and configure the container-native Factory through Office, including first-run enrollment, provider settings, project import and a deterministic authorized journey.
user_actions: complete first-run enrollment with the protected local five-minute confirmation code
retain an HttpOnly browser session across reloads
recover locally by revoking sessions and issuing a new confirmation code
save, test, revoke and audit provider credentials
import an HTTPS Git Project and configure its scope
create a typed Action and a scoped delegation
authorize and dispatch a deterministic Campaign
inspect the candidate and Quality Gate
CAP-045.notes: The deterministic fixture path is the PR CI acceptance path. The owner-authorized live OpenCode container UAT is recorded separately and is not a browser-acceptance gate.

CAP-054.name: Personal access and device sessions
CAP-054.job: Enroll a browser without a permanent API token, maintain independent device sessions, pair a phone with owner approval, and inspect optional private Tailscale access.
user_actions: complete first-run enrollment through the one-time local confirmation
inspect local and optional private remote access state
create a short-lived QR pairing challenge with a non-authorizing public identifier
compare verification codes and approve or reject a pending device
cancel an unclaimed or approved-awaiting-pickup challenge
revoke a single device, sign out the current device, or revoke all sessions
inspect bounded session and pairing security activity
CAP-054.notes: Session cookie material is HttpOnly. CSRF uses the dedicated readable SameSite cookie. Pairing challenge IDs do not grant authority and are stripped from browser history before phone requests. The phone receives a separate hashed poll capability, and Core creates a session only after the authenticated owner submits the matching code. The PWA service worker uses network-only requests; no offline authorization or sensitive-response caching is claimed. Access & Devices marks the current device, supports per-device and all-device revocation, shows bounded security activity, and cancels challenges explicitly. Tailscale status follows Core's private Office health probe and remains UNKNOWN when the probe is inconclusive. Author-run deterministic and real Chromium pairing evidence passed at implementation 9afbb6f; mobile-data Tailscale access, independent review and Product Owner approval remain pending.

Repository-backed docs require a bounded read-only projection and provenance; editing remains governed through Actions.
